A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdvI2I research, with matching authors, methods and core experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success measurements, defense comparisons, transfer experiments, ablations and qualitative examples in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds model-transfer, image-quality, safety-checker, purification, extremism and defensive-application evaluations.

M1.justification: The concept-vector construction, VAE generator, latent-matching objective, clipping and adaptive training remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 explicitly includes the safety-checker vision encoder, whose feature-comparison role was already described in v1. The additional concepts and defensive application reuse the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained nudity and violence tasks, v3 evaluates political extremism in Appendix G and introduces suppression of explicit-prompt attacks using benign image conditioning in Appendix I. These substantially broaden task coverage, while the original image-text dataset remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The principal Attack VAE, MMA and text-filter comparisons remain. v3 adds Face-Adapter to the image-quality comparison, DiffPure as a purification defense, and a ViT-B/32 safety checker in Tables 15, 17 and 13, respectively. These are focused extensions of the comparison methods.

E3.justification: v3 introduces additional model and checker configurations, transfer-under-defense evaluations, image-quality metrics including LPIPS, SSIM, TOPIQ and FID, and an original-image versus benign-conditioned-image control. The original 1800/200 training/evaluation split is retained. Newly disclosed SLD parameters do not establish that the earlier experiments used different settings or were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial investigations of transfer under defenses, transfer to different safety checkers, perceptual-quality tradeoffs, DiffPure robustness and potential defensive use. The existing generator ablation and concept-strength sweep are retained as Tables 10–11, corresponding to v1 Tables 8–9.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 and the relocated ablation tables retain their numerical results. Table 7 changes all eight ASRs, including AdvI2I transfer to SDv2.1 from 86.0% to 84.0% and SDv3.0 from 36.0% to 34.0%. New results include 74.0% FLUX transfer, 72.5% ASR under DiffPure, image-quality measurements, and a 96.5% versus 24.5% ASR comparison within the new defensive experiment.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises the formal safety-checker loss to apply the vision encoder V to the decoded image before comparison with concept embeddings. This corrects an omitted operation in the written expression, although Equation (3) remains unchanged. No new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: text filters detect existing prompt attacks, image-conditioned attacks expose an overlooked vulnerability, and adaptive attacks bypass safeguards. The expanded appendix evidence does not redefine these principal contributions.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the architectural explanation for weak SDv3.0 transfer with a conjecture about filtered training data, explicitly conditioning attack applicability on the model's existing NSFW capability. It removes the earlier architecture/resolution rationale for omitting InstructPix2Pix transfer and adds interpretations concerning image-quality tradeoffs, generator-based purification robustness and potential defensive use.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies five SLD parameters, identifies the ViT-L/14 safety checker and names the TOPIQ evaluation checkpoints. It removes v1's 256x256 resolution statement and Table 6's explicit InstructPix2Pix identification. The code-access link is unchanged; these disclosures do not establish changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for TOPIQ, rectified-flow transformers, Face-Adapter and DiffPure to support the appendix evaluations and revised transfer interpretation. The main related-work discussion and positioning of AdvI2I against prompt-based attacks remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording clarifications, introductory revisions, an expanded conclusion and a new generic Impact Statement. Appendix A.1–A.2 becomes B–C within an expanded appendix structure. The main section order and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The single-column ICLR-style presentation becomes an ICML-style two-column main text. Existing figures are enlarged and repositioned, Algorithm 1 is reflowed, and Tables 5–6 appear side by side. Nine additional appendix tables materially expand the visual presentation; the two existing figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v1 supported image fidelity mainly through constraints and examples; v3 adds quantitative quality measurements and tests against alternative safety checkers and purification defenses, addressing important gaps in the evidence for fidelity and robustness. Explicit SLD settings and qualified transfer explanations also help. Sparse protocols, absent uncertainty estimates and untested causal explanations remain limitations, but the central claims receive substantially broader empirical scrutiny.
